units.title: Scales and Classification of Map Scales
units.intro: Scale = map distance : ground distance. Three ways: statement (“1 cm to 1 km”), representative fraction (1:100 000), linear bar. Large scale (1:10 000) shows a small area in detail. Small scale (1:1 000 000) shows a big area with little detail.

cards.title: 6.1 Classification of Map Scales
body: Small Scale Maps: This group of map have scales that are smaller than 1:250,000 (like 1:1,000,000).
A city map (like the map of Asmara), land use map of a village, map of a farm, plan map of an airport are all examples of large scale maps.
Represent the farm by a map that is 5 cm long and 5 cm wide.
First, measure the map distance between two consecutive lines of latitude.
A pantograph is an instrument used to enlarge or reduce maps.

cards.title: Finding Scale of a Map When it is not given
body: If the printed scale is missing: use a known ground distance between two points. Reducing a map: scale denominator grows (less detail). Enlarging: denominator shrinks.

cards.title: Large scale, large detail
body: Think “large objects on the page.” A town plan is large-scale. A world map is small-scale.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: Which of the following formulas correctly represents the mathematical calculation of a map scale?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Recall the definition of map scale.**
Map scale is the ratio of map distance (MD) to ground distance (GD).

**Step 2: Identify the corresponding formula.**
This is mathematically expressed as $$\text{Scale} = \frac{\text{MD}}{\text{GD}}$$.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Thus, the correct option is **Scale = MD / GD**.

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: If a map is physically reduced in size, what happens to its scale?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Analyze scale changes during reduction.**
When a map is reduced, its physical dimensions decrease.

**Step 2: Connect to the scale ratio.**
This reduction increases the denominator of the RF, which means the scale becomes smaller.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Therefore, the correct option is **The scale becomes smaller.**

cards.title: Quick check
cards.q: What is the meaning of '1' in the numerator of a Representative Fraction (RF) scale?
cards.why:
**Step 1: Check the properties of an RF scale.**
In an RF scale ($$\frac{1}{\text{Denominator}}$$), the numerator represents map distance.

**Step 2: Identify the correct option.**
The value "1" represents the Map Distance.

**Step 3: Final Result**
Thus, the correct option is **The map distance**.

glossary.meaning: Where MD means map distance and GD means ground distance.

tips.text: Maps contain certain elements, which guide users to use them properly.
Maps are drawn to scale, because they are drawn on sheets of papers that are much smaller than the area they represent.
Map scale is shown in Word Statement, Representative Fraction or graphic form.
Depending on their scale, maps are classified into small, medium or large scale maps.
Small maps can be enlarged and large maps can be reduced in size.
Enlargement or reduction changes map scale and area.
When instruments are not available, the grid method can be used to enlarge or reduce maps.
